Replay

RTC continuation during a gameplay reconnect

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Relay outage evidenceReplacing a peer connection under the same ID

Use RTC continuation to preserve an authenticated signaling reservation when replacing a gameplay transport within the same authority term. Rtc_Continuation contains the existing logical peer ID, opaque room code, resume token and host/client role. It is in-memory transport state, not a membership credential, checkpoint or save.

rtc_continuation exports it only from a registered context without a terminal error, with authenticated resumption enabled. Rtc_Config.continuation accepts it only for the exact room and role, with a nonzero token and a valid peer ID. Opening still performs the provider's fresh challenge and authorization proof. The provider checks the current registered member identity and reservation token before accepting the old logical ID. Knowledge of a peer ID or room name alone grants nothing.

session_redirect uses this path only when the authority epoch, member incarnation, signaling URL and room code match the previous RTC context. New authority terms and different destinations use normal fresh connections. The new adapter asks to replace the old channels; it does not treat incomplete fragment/channel state as delivered. The client runtime remains in place, preserving action IDs and old presentation history for normal Welcome reconciliation.

An expired or rejected continuation does not confer a lease or revive an old identity. Ordinary coordinator, registration, packet-generation and authority checks remain in force. A subsequent retry may establish a fresh signaling reservation under those rules. This is distinct from the existing signaling-only reconnect, which can preserve healthy data channels without replacing them.

Relay outage evidence#

The real relay-outage fixture keeps the coordinator and both game processes alive, stops Coturn, restarts it with the same configuration and requires a newly selected relay connection with traffic in both directions. It then verifies a new guest action from the authority, unchanged incarnations/epoch and retained inventory. Logical RTC peer identity and signaling continuation are checked separately from the browser's newly constructed peer-connection index.

The initial implementation already recovered correctly, but full reconnect dropped the signaling token and could wait through the provider's reservation window. The continuation path avoids that unnecessary re-admission. Individual measured runs are recorded, not treated as a latency benchmark or an Internet guarantee. The existing 10-second gameplay timeout and platform ICE failure detection still contribute to interruption.

See recorded outage results and TURN fixture commands. Credential refresh, ICE restart, combined coordinator/relay outages, public deployment and other platform/browser envelopes remain separate work.

Replacing a peer connection under the same ID#

The public and raw RTC transports expose the peer-connection serial as local connection-generation metadata. Fragment assembly/delivery state and outer Replay Delay/Router queues retire work from the old generation. A provider's replacement introduction can therefore create fresh channels under the same numeric ID without splicing old fragments or treating old delivery frontiers as belonging to the new connection. Signaling-only continuation of healthy channels retains its generation.

The authenticated Duel tests creator recovery: the creator saves and pauses, its browser is killed, and a fresh authenticated browser restores its file. The joining browser retains its runner through timeout and reconnects when creator ID 1 changes generation. Both reach the reference world with correct occurrences. The admission service and fixed match remain alive; this does not elect another player to supply the missing creator's inputs or recover an incompatible archive.
